title: Future forms: will, going to and the present
titleVi: Các cách diễn đạt tương lai
summary: Chọn đúng cách nói về tương lai: quyết định tức thời, dự định trước, sắp xếp cố định và lịch trình.
whyItMatters: Tiếng Anh không có một 'thì tương lai' duy nhất, mà có bốn cách diễn đạt phổ biến. Trong Task 2 bạn dự đoán hệ quả (*will*), trong Speaking bạn nói về kế hoạch (*going to*) và lịch hẹn (*present continuous*). Dùng sai dạng khiến người nghe hiểu sai mức độ chắc chắn của kế hoạch.

sections.heading: will: decisions made now, offers and predictions
body: Use **will + infinitive** when the decision is made at the moment of speaking, when you offer to do something, or when you make a prediction based on opinion rather than evidence.
*I'll help you with that bag* is not a plan; it is a spontaneous offer. *The policy will probably reduce emissions* is a prediction, not a certainty.
**Will** also carries promises, refusals and formal statements: *The government will invest a further 2 billion dollars.*

examples.right: I'll send you the report this afternoon.
examples.note: Decision made now, in response to a request.

examples.right: Higher fees will probably deter poorer applicants.
examples.note: Prediction based on opinion — softened by **probably**.

examples.right: I won't accept the offer unless the salary improves.

sections.heading: going to: prior plans and evidence-based predictions
body: Use **be going to + infinitive** when the decision was made before speaking, or when the present situation makes the future obvious.
*I'm going to apply for a master's degree* means I had already decided. *Look at those clouds — it's going to rain* means the evidence is visible now.
The distinction between *will* and *going to* is often a matter of intention rather than grammar, but examiners notice the difference in Speaking Part 1 when you talk about plans.

examples.right: I'm going to apply for a master's degree next year.
Look at the traffic — we're going to be late.
The council is going to ban cars from the old quarter.
examples.note: An announced intention, treated as settled.

sections.heading: Present continuous and present simple for the future
body: Use the present continuous for a fixed personal arrangement with a time and usually another person: *I'm meeting my supervisor on Friday.*
Use the present simple for timetables and schedules — transport, exams, term dates: *The exam starts at 9 a.m.* Using *will start* here sounds foreign.
This is the highest-frequency source of error in Speaking Part 1, where candidates often answer *I will meet my friend tomorrow* when they mean an arrangement that already exists.

rows: I'm going to take the earlier train.
I'm taking the earlier train tomorrow.

sections.heading: Choosing between will and going to
body: The practical rule: if you can add *I've decided* before the verb, use **going to**. If you can add *I've just decided*, use **will**.

Predictions split the same way. With no evidence, **will** is normal (*I think rents will fall*); with visible evidence, **going to** is stronger (*Rents are going to fall — three landlords have already cut prices*).
In formal writing, **will** is the safer default for projections; **going to** can sound conversational.

examples.right: I've decided — I'm going to take the job.
That's a good idea. I'll take the job.
examples.note: Decision made at the moment of speaking.

examples.right: The report predicts that demand will double by 2035.
examples.wrong: The report predicts that demand is going to double by 2035.
examples.note: Dự báo học thuật dùng **will** trang trọng hơn.

sections.heading: Talking about the future in IELTS
body: Task 1 sometimes shows a projection to a future year. Report projections with **is expected to**, **is projected to**, **is set to** rather than a bare future tense — this is the register of a band 7.5+ report.
Task 2 predictions should be hedged. *Will* alone sounds overconfident: *Urbanisation will destroy...* Better: *Urbanisation is likely to put further pressure on...*
In Speaking Part 3, mix the forms naturally: a plan in **going to**, a prediction in **will**, an arrangement in the present continuous.

examples.right: The population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050.
Automation is likely to displace millions of routine jobs.
I'm flying to Singapore next month, and I think the conference will be useful.
examples.note: Arrangement + prediction in one natural sentence.

commonMistakes.wrong: When I will arrive, I will call you.
commonMistakes.right: When I arrive, I will call you.
commonMistakes.why: Mệnh đề thời gian với `when`, `after`, `before`, `as soon as` không dùng `will`. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến vì người học dịch 'khi tôi sẽ đến'.

commonMistakes.wrong: Look at those clouds. It will rain.
commonMistakes.right: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
commonMistakes.why: Khi có bằng chứng trước mắt, dùng `be going to`. `Will` dành cho dự đoán dựa trên ý kiến.

commonMistakes.wrong: I will meet my supervisor at 3 p.m. tomorrow — we fixed it last week.
commonMistakes.right: I'm meeting my supervisor at 3 p.m. tomorrow — we fixed it last week.
commonMistakes.why: Sắp xếp đã cố định với thời gian cụ thể dùng `present continuous`, không dùng `will`.
Lịch trình giao thông cố định dùng `present simple`. `Will` khiến câu nghe như một dự đoán về tương lai.

commonMistakes.wrong: I am going to can speak Japanese after the course.
commonMistakes.right: I am going to be able to speak Japanese after the course.
commonMistakes.why: Không dùng hai modal liền nhau. `Can` không có dạng tương lai, phải thay bằng `be able to`.

ieltsTips: Trong Task 1 có số liệu dự báo, ưu tiên `is/are projected to`, `is expected to`, `is set to` — giọng học thuật và an toàn hơn `will`.
Trong Task 2, luôn giảm nhẹ dự đoán: `will` + trạng từ (`probably`, `likely to`) hoặc `may/might` để tránh khẳng định quá tuyệt đối.
Trong Speaking Part 1, phân biệt rõ kế hoạch (`going to`) và sắp xếp đã cố định (`present continuous`) — giám khảo đánh giá đây là dấu hiệu kiểm soát thì.
Ghi nhớ: sau `when/if/before/after/as soon as` không dùng `will`; dùng `present simple` cho mệnh đề thời gian và điều kiện.

exercises.question: Look at those dark clouds. It ___.
exercises.explanation: Bằng chứng trước mắt → **be going to**.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the present simple correctly after 'when' for a future event?
options: When I will arrive, I will call you.
When I arrive, I will call you.
When I arrive, I call you.
When I will arrive, I call you.
exercises.explanation: Mệnh đề thời gian sau **when** dùng **present simple**, mệnh đề chính dùng **will**.

exercises.question: The timetable says the exam ___ at 9 a.m.
exercises.explanation: Lịch trình chính thức dùng **present simple**.

exercises.question: A colleague is struggling with a heavy box. You say:
options: I'm going to help you with that.
exercises.explanation: Lời đề nghị ứng khẩu tại thời điểm nói → **will**.

exercises.question: Which sentence reports an academic projection in the right register?
options: The population will be 9.7 billion by 2050.
The population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050.
The population is going to be 9.7 billion by 2050.
exercises.explanation: **be projected to** là cấu trúc chuẩn trong báo cáo học thuật.

exercises.question: We ___ (fly) to Singapore next Thursday — the tickets are already booked.
exercises.explanation: Sắp xếp cố định có thời gian cụ thể → present continuous.

exercises.question: I've decided — I ___ (study) in Australia next year.
exercises.explanation: Quyết định có từ trước → **be going to**.

exercises.question: Don't worry about the invoice — I ___ (send) it this afternoon.
exercises.explanation: Quyết định tại thời điểm nói, dạng lời hứa → **will**.

exercises.question: As soon as the results ___ (come) out, I will let you know.
exercises.hint: as soon as + mệnh đề thời gian
exercises.explanation: Sau **as soon as** dùng present simple, không dùng **will**.

exercises.question: The report ___ (predict) that demand will double by 2035.
exercises.hint: the report + nội dung dự báo
exercises.explanation: Động từ tường thuật ở hiện tại đơn; mệnh đề sau giữ **will** cho dự báo.
